title: A Major Overhaul of Prescription Drug Prices

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带上300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: A year ago, Congress overhauled the way drugs for older Americans get paid for by giving Medicare the power to bargain with drug makers over prices.
sentences.zh: 一年前，国会通过赋予联邦医疗保险（Medicare）与制药商协商药品价格的权力，彻底改变了美国老年人支付药费的方式。

sentences.en: It was the biggest change in health care in more than a decade.
sentences.zh: 这是十多年来医疗保健领域最大的变革。

sentences.en: This week, the Biden administration began to implement it.
sentences.zh: 本周，拜登政府开始实施这一政策。

sentences.en: My colleagues, Cheryl Stolberg, on the decades-long battle to get that power.
sentences.zh: 我的同事谢丽尔·斯托尔伯格将讲述这场争取该权力的数十年斗争。

sentences.en: And Rebecca Robbins on its potential to reshape the business of drugs in America.
sentences.zh: 丽贝卡·罗宾斯将探讨其重塑美国药品行业的潜力。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, August 31St.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月31日，星期四。

sentences.en: So, Cheryl, there's a very big change underway with Medicare, which is, of course, the government health insurance program for older Americans.
sentences.zh: 那么，谢丽尔，联邦医疗保险正在进行一项非常重大的变革，当然，这是政府为美国老年人提供的医疗保险计划。

sentences.en: And I immediately thought of you, my former D.C.
sentences.zh: 我立刻想到了你，我以前在华盛顿的同事，

sentences.en: colleague and longtime health care policy reporter.
sentences.zh: 也是资深的医疗保健政策记者。

sentences.en: Tell me what's going on.
sentences.zh: 告诉我发生了什么。

sentences.en: So, the administration announced its plans to have Medicare negotiate directly with drug makers for the first time ever over the price of medicines to basically bargain them down.
sentences.zh: 政府宣布了计划，首次让联邦医疗保险直接与制药商就药品价格进行谈判，基本上是为了压低价格。

sentences.en: So, it's going to start kind of small.
sentences.zh: 所以，起步规模会比较小。

sentences.en: The White House announced 10 drugs.
sentences.zh: 白宫公布了10种药品。

sentences.en: These are drugs for diabetes and stroke and heart disease and arthritis and cancer whose prices will be subject to Medicare negotiations.
sentences.zh: 这些是用于治疗糖尿病、中风、心脏病、关节炎和癌症的药物，其价格将受到联邦医疗保险谈判的约束。

sentences.en: It's really a paradigm shift and it opens the door toward more and more drugs being subject to price negotiations.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个范式转移，它为未来越来越多的药品接受价格谈判打开了大门。

sentences.en: And it's a huge deal.
sentences.zh: 这是一件大事。

sentences.en: It's the biggest change to the health care system in this country since the passage of the Affordable Care Act in 2010.
sentences.zh: 这是自2010年《平价医疗法案》通过以来，美国医疗保健系统最大的变革。

sentences.en: And what's the goal here?
sentences.zh: 那么，目标是什么呢？

sentences.en: So, the goal is pretty simple.
sentences.zh: 目标很简单。

sentences.en: It's to lower drug prices.
sentences.zh: 就是降低药价。

sentences.en: Americans pay the highest drug prices of anywhere in the developed world.
sentences.zh: 美国人支付的药价是发达国家中最高的。

sentences.en: There was a study by the RAND Corporation that found that drug prices in the United States are two and a half times those of comparable countries.
sentences.zh: 兰德公司的一项研究发现，美国的药价是同类国家的两倍半。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, help us understand why this is such a shift, Cheryl.
sentences.zh: 那么，谢丽尔，请帮我们理解为什么这是一个如此巨大的转变。

sentences.en: Like, how had Medicare functioned up until now when it comes to prescription drugs?
sentences.zh: 在处方药方面，联邦医疗保险到目前为止是如何运作的？

sentences.en: So, it might be hard to remember, but for much of Medicare's history, there was no coverage of prescription drugs.
sentences.zh: 可能很难记起来了，但在联邦医疗保险历史的大部分时间里，它是不覆盖处方药的。

sentences.en: Older people would go broke paying for their medicine.
sentences.zh: 老年人会因为支付药费而破产。

sentences.en: You know, there were these horror stories of people choosing, you know, between food and drugs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有很多关于人们在食物和药品之间做选择的恐怖故事。

sentences.en: And I actually asked my own mom yesterday, what did you do before Medicare covered drugs?
sentences.zh: 我昨天还问了我妈妈，在联邦医疗保险覆盖药品之前你们是怎么做的？

sentences.en: And she said, we just paid for them out of pocket.
sentences.zh: 她说，我们只能自掏腰包。

sentences.en: She said, my dad had been on chemotherapy and they were paying $300 a pill.
sentences.zh: 她说，我父亲当时在做化疗，他们每片药要付300美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And they were on cholesterol drugs.
sentences.zh: 他们还要吃降胆固醇的药。

sentences.en: And they had figured out a way to get them from Canada where it was cheaper.
sentences.zh: 他们想办法从加拿大买，那里便宜些。

sentences.en: So, this was how Medicare functioned for decades.
sentences.zh: 这就是联邦医疗保险几十年来运作的方式。

sentences.en: When did it become part of the political debate?
sentences.zh: 它是什么时候成为政治辩论的一部分的？

sentences.en: So, it really became a big part of the political debate in 2000 when Al Gore was running against George Bush for the presidency.
sentences.zh: 它真正成为政治辩论的重要组成部分是在2000年，当时阿尔·戈尔正在与乔治·布什竞选总统。

sentences.en: And Gore, who was vice president, was just railing against the drug companies and making a big push.
sentences.zh: 身为副总统的戈尔当时猛烈抨击制药公司，并大力推动改革。

sentences.en: It's embarrassing that we have senior citizens getting on buses and going to Canada in order to get more affordable prescription drugs.
sentences.zh: 我们有老年人不得不坐大巴去加拿大购买更实惠的处方药，这真是令人尴尬。

sentences.en: Gore wanted the government to do something about this.
sentences.zh: 戈尔希望政府对此采取行动。

sentences.en: He wanted to expand Medicare to cover drugs.
sentences.zh: 他希望扩大联邦医疗保险的覆盖范围，将药品纳入其中。

sentences.en: It is long past time to take on the big drug companies and say, it is time for a prescription drug benefit for all seniors under the Medicare program.
sentences.zh: 现在是时候对付那些大型制药公司了，是时候为联邦医疗保险计划下的所有老年人提供处方药福利了。

sentences.en: All seniors.
sentences.zh: 所有老年人。

sentences.en: So, on the campaign trail, Gore was just hammering Bush about this.
sentences.zh: 所以，在竞选活动中，戈尔一直在就这个问题猛烈抨击布什。

sentences.en: My opponent is supported by the HMOs and the insurance companies and the big drug companies.
sentences.zh: 我的对手得到了健康维护组织、保险公司和大型制药公司的支持。

sentences.en: And he has taken their position opposing these measures.
sentences.zh: 他采取了他们的立场，反对这些措施。

sentences.en: And Bush was coming back and saying, well, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 布什反击说，等一下。

sentences.en: You know, we've got a plan, too.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们也有计划。

sentences.en: I mean, we need to have a modern system to help seniors.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们需要一个现代化的系统来帮助老年人。

sentences.en: But our plan isn't a government plan.
sentences.zh: 但我们的计划不是政府计划。

sentences.en: Our plan is a private plan.
sentences.zh: 我们的计划是私人计划。

sentences.en: We want to rely on private insurance companies to sell drug coverage policies to older people.
sentences.zh: 我们希望依靠私人保险公司向老年人销售药品保险政策。

sentences.en: And the idea of supporting a federally controlled 132,000 page document bureaucracy as being a compassionate way for seniors is just not my vision.
sentences.zh: 而支持一个由联邦控制的、长达13.2万页的官僚机构作为关怀老年人的方式，这根本不是我的愿景。

sentences.en: I believe we ought to give seniors more options.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们应该给老年人更多的选择。

sentences.en: I believe we ought to make the system work better.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们应该让这个系统运作得更好。

sentences.en: And it would be backed by kind of government subsidies and incentives.
sentences.zh: 它将得到政府补贴和激励措施的支持。

sentences.en: So, both parties really agreed that something had to be done.
sentences.zh: 所以，两党其实都同意必须采取行动。

sentences.en: Let me ask you both this and we'll move on on this subject.
sentences.zh: 让我问你们俩一个问题，然后我们就继续讨论这个话题。

sentences.en: As a practical matter, both of you want to bring prescription drugs to seniors, correct?
sentences.zh: 从实际角度来看，你们俩都想为老年人提供处方药，对吧？

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They were just fighting over how to do it.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在争论如何实现这一点。

sentences.en: The difference is I want to bring it to 100 percent and he brings it only to 5 percent.
sentences.zh: 区别在于，我想让覆盖率达到100%，而他只覆盖了5%。

sentences.en: That's just totally false.
sentences.zh: 这完全是错误的。

sentences.en: Wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: It's just totally false.
sentences.zh: 这完全是错误的。

sentences.en: OK, so Bush, of course, gets elected.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以布什当然当选了。

sentences.en: What does he do with this campaign promise?
sentences.zh: 他如何处理这个竞选承诺？

sentences.en: So, I was covering this at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在报道这件事。

sentences.en: And what Bush did was he decided that he was going to kind of leave it up to Congress to come up with the details.
sentences.zh: 布什决定把细节留给国会去处理。

sentences.en: And then we suddenly had a political alignment not seen since the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 然后我们突然出现了一种自20世纪50年代以来从未见过的政治格局。

sentences.en: Republicans were in charge of the White House, the House, and the Senate.
sentences.zh: 共和党人掌控了白宫、众议院和参议院。

sentences.en: And this issue, drug prices, was pending before them at the request of the president.
sentences.zh: 而这个问题，即药价问题，正应总统的要求摆在他们面前。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, Republicans had total control of all branches of government.
sentences.zh: 所以，共和党人完全控制了政府的所有部门。

sentences.en: So, effectively, the go-ahead for this potential policy that Bush had in mind.
sentences.zh: 因此，实际上，布什心目中的这项潜在政策得到了绿灯。

sentences.en: Well, Republicans might have had control of everything, but they didn't have the votes to pass the private kind of plan that most of them would have wanted.
sentences.zh: 嗯，共和党人可能控制了一切，但他们没有足够的票数通过他们大多数人想要的私人计划。

sentences.en: So, there were a lot of negotiations, a lot of back and forth.
sentences.zh: 所以，经过了很多谈判，很多来回拉锯。

sentences.en: And one of the key drivers of this debate was this Louisiana congressman named Billy Towson.
sentences.zh: 这场辩论的关键推动者之一是来自路易斯安那州的国会议员比利·托森。

sentences.en: The gentleman from Louisiana, Mr. Towson.
sentences.zh: 来自路易斯安那州的绅士，托森先生。

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. Chairman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢主席先生。

sentences.en: Let me first acknowledge that this is an historic meeting of the House and Senate on what has become an issue to so many senior citizens across the country.
sentences.zh: 首先，我要承认，这是众议院和参议院的一次历史性会议，讨论的是全国这么多老年人关心的问题。

sentences.en: He was kind of a point man, if you will.
sentences.zh: 他算是牵头人，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: He was chairman of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, and he had a huge role in drafting this legislation.
sentences.zh: 他是众议院能源和商业委员会主席，在起草这项立法中发挥了巨大作用。

sentences.en: And if we miss that opportunity because we fail to come together in agreement and give the president a chance to sign a bill, shame on us.
sentences.zh: 如果我们因为未能达成一致、未能给总统签署法案的机会而错失良机，那真是我们的耻辱。

sentences.en: But there was a big stumbling block.
sentences.zh: 但有一个巨大的绊脚石。

sentences.en: President Bush is urging Congress to pass a Medicare prescription drug bill, but deep divisions remain on Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 布什总统敦促国会通过一项联邦医疗保险处方药法案，但国会内部仍存在严重分歧。

sentences.en: The House bill relies much more heavily on private insurance plans that would compete directly with traditional Medicare.
sentences.zh: 众议院的法案更多地依赖于与传统联邦医疗保险直接竞争的私人保险计划。

sentences.en: Democrats opposed it vehemently.
sentences.zh: 民主党人强烈反对。

sentences.en: Boy, do they have a prescription for you.
sentences.zh: 天哪，他们确实为你准备了一份处方。

sentences.en: Further weakening the foundation of Medicare for the seniors who need it moSt.
sentences.zh: 进一步削弱了最需要联邦医疗保险的老年人的保障基础。

sentences.en: You know, GOP used to stand for grand old party.
sentences.zh: 你知道，共和党（GOP）过去代表“大老党”。

sentences.en: Now it stands for get old people.
sentences.zh: 现在它代表“搞定老年人”。

sentences.en: I'm offended that anyone would come to this floor and accuse anyone in this House of wanting to get old people.
sentences.zh: 我被冒犯了，竟然有人来到这个议会大厅，指责本院的任何人想要“搞定老年人”。

sentences.en: Do you think for a second you love your moms and dads any more than we love ours?
sentences.zh: 你以为你们爱自己的父母比我们爱我们的父母多一秒吗？

sentences.en: So what happens is, through negotiations back and forth, they come up with this plan for Medicare to actually expand to cover prescription drugs.
sentences.zh: 所以发生的事情是，通过来回谈判，他们提出了这个计划，让联邦医疗保险真正扩大到覆盖处方药。

sentences.en: But there's a catch.
sentences.zh: 但有一个陷阱。

sentences.en: And the catch is that there is what they call the non-interference clause.
sentences.zh: 陷阱就是他们所说的“不干预条款”。

sentences.en: What's that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: The non-interference clause, which the drug companies desperately wanted,
sentences.zh: 制药公司极力想要这个“不干预条款”，

sentences.en: explicitly barred the federal government from directly negotiating drug prices with the pharmaceutical manufacturers.
sentences.zh: 它明确禁止联邦政府直接与制药商协商药品价格。

sentences.en: So it means effectively that the government is providing this benefit with one hand tied behind its back.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上意味着政府在提供这项福利时，等于是自缚双手。

sentences.en: Because it can't use its bargaining power to drive down prices.
sentences.zh: 因为它不能利用其议价能力来压低价格。

sentences.en: So you've got this kind of sprawling system of individual insurers who could bargain with the companies.
sentences.zh: 所以你拥有一个庞大的个人保险公司系统，他们可以与公司讨价还价。

sentences.en: But Medicare as a whole couldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 但联邦医疗保险作为一个整体却不能这样做。

sentences.en: This big, giant agency that was responsible for insuring millions and millions of Americans, they couldn't get together and bargain as one.
sentences.zh: 这个负责为数百万美国人提供保险的庞大机构，却无法联合起来进行统一谈判。

sentences.en: Yeah, and the drug industry wanted nothing to do with having the government negotiate their prices.
sentences.zh: 是的，制药行业根本不想让政府协商他们的价格。

sentences.en: The drug industry has a lot of lobbyists.
sentences.zh: 制药行业有很多游说者。

sentences.en: Some people will tell you they have three lobbyists for every member of Congress.
sentences.zh: 有些人会告诉你，他们平均每位国会议员就有三名游说者。

sentences.en: The members of Congress are elected, but, you know, the lobbyists have a certain degree of power.
sentences.zh: 国会议员是民选的，但你知道，游说者拥有一定的权力。

sentences.en: So essentially, the plan they came up with ended up being all carrot and no stick, effectively, right?
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，他们提出的计划最终变成了只有胡萝卜没有大棒，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, the government is saying to drug makers, here you go.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，政府对制药商说，给你。

sentences.en: Here's a massive new pool of customers.
sentences.zh: 这里有一大群新的客户。

sentences.en: But we can't use any of our clout as this giant drug buyer, right?
sentences.zh: 但我们不能利用我们作为这个巨大药品买家的任何影响力，对吧？

sentences.en: This 800-pound gorilla that is Medicare to demand lower prices.
sentences.zh: 联邦医疗保险这个800磅重的大猩猩，却不能要求更低的价格。

sentences.en: So American taxpayers end up footing this really big new bill.
sentences.zh: 所以美国纳税人最终要承担这笔巨大的新账单。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So it seems like a big giveaway to the drug industry.
sentences.zh: 所以这看起来像是给制药行业的一份大礼。

sentences.en: Okay, so this was the proposal that Towson landed on.
sentences.zh: 好的，这就是托森最终提出的提案。

sentences.en: What did his colleagues in Congress think of it?
sentences.zh: 他在国会的同事们是怎么看的？

sentences.en: Well, it satisfied some Republicans, but not enough.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它满足了一些共和党人，但还不够。

sentences.en: There was a lot of pushback within the party.
sentences.zh: 党内有很多反对声音。

sentences.en: This would be the biggest new federal entitlement since 1965, when Medicare was created.
sentences.zh: 这将是自1965年联邦医疗保险创建以来最大的联邦福利项目。

sentences.en: Conservative Republicans didn't like the idea of a major expansion of a government program, much less an entitlement program like Medicare.
sentences.zh: 保守派共和党人不喜欢大幅扩张政府项目的想法，更不用说像联邦医疗保险这样的福利项目了。

sentences.en: Let us not in this Congress today sow the seeds to destroy the foundation of a free market system.
sentences.zh: 让我们不要在今天的国会中播下摧毁自由市场体系基础的种子。

sentences.en: Nonetheless, the bill comes to a vote.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，该法案还是付诸表决了。

sentences.en: They actually started the roll call vote at 3 a.m.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上在凌晨3点开始了点名表决，

sentences.en: after a lot of back-and-forth debate and nervousness about whether or not this thing was going to pass.
sentences.zh: 在经过了大量的来回辩论和对该法案是否能通过的紧张不安之后。

sentences.en: The quarter vote is ordered.
sentences.zh: 点名表决已下令进行。

sentences.en: The A's and A's are ordered.
sentences.zh: 已下令进行赞成票和反对票的登记。

sentences.en: This will be a 15-minute vote.
sentences.zh: 这将是一次15分钟的投票。

sentences.en: It was supposed to be a 15-minute vote.
sentences.zh: 这本应是一次15分钟的投票。

sentences.en: Instead, it took hours.
sentences.zh: 结果却花了几个小时。

sentences.en: You're watching live coverage of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你正在观看C-SPAN对美国众议院的现场报道。

sentences.en: House of Representatives on C-SPAN.
sentences.zh: 这次投票开始于东部时间凌晨3点，

sentences.en: This vote started at 3 a.m.
sentences.zh: 大约是一个小时20分钟前。

sentences.en: Eastern, about an hour and 20 minutes ago.
sentences.zh: 你知道，布什在凌晨时分给共和党人打电话。

sentences.en: You know, Bush was calling Republicans in the wee hours of the morning.
sentences.zh: 还有其他议员希望改变他们的投票吗？

sentences.en: Any other members wish to change their votes?
sentences.zh: 当时的众议院多数党领袖汤姆·迪莱也在施加压力。

sentences.en: Tom DeLay, the House majority leader at the time, was also twisting arMs.
sentences.zh: 投票持续了太久，以至于一些国会议员竟然睡着了。

sentences.en: It went on so long that some members of Congress actually fell asleep.
sentences.zh: 毕竟已经是凌晨3点了。

sentences.en: I mean, it was 3 a.m.
sentences.zh: 投票直到早上6点才结束。

sentences.en: after all.
sentences.zh: 在这次投票中，赞成票为220票，反对票为215票。

sentences.en: And the vote didn't close until 6 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 会议工作在无异议的情况下获得通过。

sentences.en: On this vote, the A's are 2-20, the A's are 2-15.
sentences.zh: （注：原文148与149对应内容调整以符合逻辑）

sentences.zh: （注：原文148与149对应内容调整以符合逻辑）

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Thanks for the warm welcome.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家的热情欢迎。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: In a few moments, I will have the honor...
sentences.zh: 再过一会儿，我将有幸……

sentences.en: Shortly thereafter, on December 8, 2003...
sentences.zh: 此后不久，即2003年12月8日……

sentences.en: ...of signing an historic act of Congress into law.
sentences.zh: ……签署一项具有历史意义的国会法案，使其成为法律。

sentences.en: President Bush signs this landmark legislation into law.
sentences.zh: 布什总统签署了这项具有里程碑意义的立法。

sentences.en: I'm pleased that all of you are here to witness the greatest advance
sentences.zh: 我很高兴在座的各位能见证这一伟大的进步，

sentences.en: in health care coverage for America's seniors since the founding of Medicare.
sentences.zh: 这是自联邦医疗保险（Medicare）创立以来，美国老年人医疗保险覆盖范围方面取得的最大进步。

sentences.en: And he said that this bill is, quote, the greatest advance in health care coverage for America's seniors since the founding of Medicare.
sentences.zh: 他说，这项法案是“自联邦医疗保险创立以来，美国老年人医疗保险覆盖范围方面取得的最大进步”。

sentences.en: So what does it look like for Medicare patients once this program is fully launched?
sentences.zh: 那么，一旦该计划全面实施，联邦医疗保险患者的情况会是怎样呢？

sentences.en: So, it's a huge relief, a big win for Medicare patients.
sentences.zh: 所以，这对联邦医疗保险患者来说是一个巨大的解脱，一场大胜。

sentences.en: But it wasn't perfect.
sentences.zh: 但它并不完美。

sentences.en: They still had to pay premiums and out-of-pocket co-pays.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然需要支付保费和自付费用。

sentences.en: And prices continued to go up.
sentences.zh: 而且价格还在持续上涨。

sentences.en: You know, from 2009 to 2018, the average price of brand name drugs for Medicare more than doubled.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从2009年到2018年，联邦医疗保险品牌药的平均价格翻了一倍多。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, people were really still feeling the pinch.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们确实仍然感到压力。

sentences.en: And this just added to the public perception that, you know, pharma had a lock on Washington.
sentences.zh: 这进一步加深了公众的看法，即制药业在华盛顿拥有垄断权。

sentences.en: And there was this feeling, I remember, Cheryl, I was covering public health at the time of, you know, why isn't the government doing something about this?
sentences.zh: 我记得当时有一种感觉，谢丽尔，我当时在报道公共卫生新闻，人们在问：为什么政府对此无动于衷？

sentences.en: These prices are crazy, you know?
sentences.zh: 这些价格太疯狂了，不是吗？

sentences.en: How can this be possible?
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能呢？

sentences.en: So, what changes?
sentences.zh: 那么，有什么变化吗？

sentences.en: Bring me to the next moment.
sentences.zh: 带我进入下一个阶段。

sentences.en: And so, in 2016, Donald Trump, of all people, was talking about this.
sentences.zh: 于是，在2016年，唐纳德·特朗普竟然也谈到了这个问题。

sentences.en: We're the largest purchaser of drugs in the world, the United States, by far.
sentences.zh: 我们是世界上最大的药品采购国，美国，遥遥领先。

sentences.en: We don't bid.
sentences.zh: 但我们却不参与竞价。

sentences.en: He was really taking on the drug industry.
sentences.zh: 他确实是在向制药业开战。

sentences.en: And he was making it a campaign issue.
sentences.zh: 他将其变成了一个竞选议题。

sentences.en: He was saying that it was crazy, that the government couldn't make a deal.
sentences.zh: 他说政府不能进行谈判是很疯狂的。

sentences.en: Because the politicians that I'm running against and others are getting tremendous campaign contributions from the pharmaceutical industry, the drug industry.
sentences.zh: 因为与我竞选的政客和其他人，从制药行业那里获得了巨额的竞选捐款。

sentences.en: And they don't want to have bidding.
sentences.zh: 他们不想进行竞价。

sentences.en: And then he continued talking about this once he got into office.
sentences.zh: 他上任后继续谈论这个问题。

sentences.en: Therefore, today, I'm signing four sweeping executive orders that will lead to massive reduction in drug costs.
sentences.zh: 因此，今天我签署了四项全面的行政命令，这将大幅降低药品成本。

sentences.en: Massive.
sentences.zh: 大幅度。

sentences.en: And in fact, toward the end of his presidency, he issued an executive order that would tie prescription drug prices in the United States to those in other developed countries.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在他任期快结束时，他发布了一项行政命令，将美国的处方药价格与其他发达国家挂钩。

sentences.en: And the pharmaceutical industry was apoplectic.
sentences.zh: 制药行业对此感到愤怒。

sentences.en: But, you know, it was an executive order, which is basically an order that the president issues.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，这只是一项行政命令，基本上就是总统发布的指令。

sentences.en: Unlike legislation, it doesn't have the authority of Congress.
sentences.zh: 与立法不同，它没有国会的授权。

sentences.en: And it didn't really change much.
sentences.zh: 它并没有真正改变太多。

sentences.en: But it certainly put the issue back on the table.
sentences.zh: 但它确实让这个问题重新回到了谈判桌上。

sentences.en: So in some way, Trump kind of takes away Republicans' cover on this issue, right?
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，特朗普在一定程度上消除了共和党在这个问题上的顾虑，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, Trump, the populist, showed that the traditional Republican position on this was not actually a view held by a large part of the Republican base.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，民粹主义者特朗普表明，共和党在这一问题上的传统立场，实际上并不被共和党的大部分选民所认同。

sentences.en: Like, people wanted the government to take action on prices.
sentences.zh: 人们希望政府在价格问题上采取行动。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And polling showed a vast majority of Americans wanted the government to take some kind of action.
sentences.zh: 民调显示，绝大多数美国人希望政府采取某种行动。

sentences.en: And so this opened a conversation among Republicans.
sentences.zh: 这开启了共和党内部的对话。

sentences.en: But more importantly, Biden gets elected and the House and the Senate are in Democratic hands.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，拜登当选了，众议院和参议院都掌握在民主党手中。

sentences.en: So now he's got the climate to do something about this.
sentences.zh: 所以现在他有了采取行动的条件。

sentences.en: And he and the Democrats in Congress put this change, this provision, to allow Medicare to negotiate drug prices.
sentences.zh: 他和国会的民主党人加入了这一变革，即允许联邦医疗保险就药品价格进行谈判的条款。

sentences.en: They put it in this sprawling bill, the Inflation Reduction Act, which tackled climate change and a lot of other things.
sentences.zh: 他们将其纳入了这项庞大的法案——《通胀削减法案》，该法案还涉及气候变化和许多其他事项。

sentences.en: And it said that by September 1st, 2023, the government shall announce the first 10 drugs to be subject to Medicare price negotiations.
sentences.zh: 法案规定，到2023年9月1日，政府应公布首批10种纳入联邦医疗保险价格谈判的药物。

sentences.en: So that's exactly what the Biden administration did.
sentences.zh: 这正是拜登政府所做的。

sentences.en: It is my greatest honor to introduce the man responsible for all these incredible changes, President Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 我非常荣幸地介绍促成所有这些惊人变革的人，乔·拜登总统。

sentences.en: Biden comes to the White House.
sentences.zh: 拜登来到白宫。

sentences.en: Unless you needed the drugs yourself or knew someone who did, it wasn't as real.
sentences.zh: 除非你自己需要这些药，或者认识需要的人，否则这感觉并不真实。

sentences.en: But boy, we've been fighting big pharma for a long time.
sentences.zh: 但天哪，我们与大型制药公司的斗争已经持续了很长时间。

sentences.en: And he says this has been a long time coming.
sentences.zh: 他说这是期待已久的时刻。

sentences.en: Today is the start of a new deal for patients where big pharma doesn't just get a blank check at your expense and the expense of the American people.
sentences.zh: 今天是患者新政的开始，大型制药公司不能再以牺牲你和美国人民的利益为代价，随意开出空白支票。

sentences.en: And, you know, we've finally taken on big pharma and we're not going to back down.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们终于向大型制药公司开战了，我们不会退缩。

sentences.en: On my watch, health care should be a right, not a privilege in this country.
sentences.zh: 在我任内，医疗保健应该是一项权利，而不是在这个国家的特权。

sentences.en: But I have to say, Sabrina, the drug industry is not going down without a fight.
sentences.zh: 但我必须说，萨布丽娜，制药行业不会束手就擒。

sentences.en: And the actual mechanics of how this will affect the pocketbooks of ordinary Americans is a lot more complicated than the president suggested at the White House on Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 而且，这实际上将如何影响普通美国人的钱包，其机制比总统周二在白宫所说的要复杂得多。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎每年都是联盟中最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受 nytimes.com/subscribe 上的特别优惠。

sentences.en: So, Rebecca, I just talked to our colleague Cheryl Stolberg and she told me the whole backstory of how this new change to Medicare came to be, where, you know,
sentences.zh: 那么，丽贝卡，我刚刚和我们的同事谢丽尔·斯托尔伯格谈过，她告诉我联邦医疗保险这一新变革背后的完整故事，你知道，

sentences.en: the government will start to now negotiate the prices of some drugs.
sentences.zh: 政府现在将开始就某些药品的价格进行谈判。

sentences.en: And because you cover the pharmaceutical industry, I wanted to talk to you about how this is all going to play out in terms of dollars and cents.
sentences.zh: 因为你负责报道制药行业，我想和你谈谈这一切在金钱方面将如何发展。

sentences.en: And really what this will mean for consumers and for the industry.
sentences.zh: 以及这对消费者和行业意味着什么。

sentences.en: So, to start with, can you tell us what drugs the government is targeting?
sentences.zh: 首先，你能告诉我们政府针对的是哪些药物吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so the government put out a list of 10 drugs that are going to be subject to negotiation.
sentences.zh: 是的，政府列出了一份包含10种将进行谈判的药物清单。

sentences.en: And these are products that are made by some of the biggest pharmaceutical companies in the world.
sentences.zh: 这些产品是由世界上一些最大的制药公司生产的。

sentences.en: Bristol-Myers Squibb, Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer, all household names.
sentences.zh: 百时美施贵宝、强生、辉瑞，都是家喻户晓的名字。

sentences.en: And the Biden administration devised the list based on a very specific set of criteria.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府根据一套非常具体的标准制定了这份清单。

sentences.en: They weren't making arbitrary choices about which products they wanted to be on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 他们并不是随意选择哪些产品应该上榜。

sentences.en: It was really based on a process that took into account a number of different factors.
sentences.zh: 这确实是基于一个考虑了多种不同因素的过程。

sentences.en: And what factors were they taking into account?
sentences.zh: 他们考虑了哪些因素？

sentences.en: For one, the products had to be widely used drugs that account for a lot of Medicare spending.
sentences.zh: 首先，这些产品必须是广泛使用的药物，且占联邦医疗保险支出的大部分。

sentences.en: So, we're talking drugs that target conditions that affect older people predominantly.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们谈论的是针对老年人常见疾病的药物。

sentences.en: One example is the blood thinner Eliquis, which prevents strokes and blood clots.
sentences.zh: 一个例子是血液稀释剂艾乐妥（Eliquis），它可以预防中风和血栓。

sentences.en: That was taken in the past year by 3.7 million people on Medicare.
sentences.zh: 去年有370万联邦医疗保险参保人服用了这种药。

sentences.en: So, really, they're targeting drugs that are in heavy rotation in the American population.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们确实是在针对美国人群中高频使用的药物。

sentences.en: And that makes sense in terms of bang for the buck, right?
sentences.zh: 从性价比的角度来看，这是有道理的，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a way to lessen the cost for the government.
sentences.zh: 这是政府降低成本的一种方式。

sentences.en: Are there other criteria that they're considering?
sentences.zh: 他们还在考虑其他标准吗？

sentences.en: So, the drugs to be eligible for negotiation have to have been on the market for a number of years.
sentences.zh: 有资格进行谈判的药物必须已经在市场上销售了若干年。

sentences.en: They're trying to target drugs at a very specific moment.
sentences.zh: 他们试图在特定的时间点针对这些药物。

sentences.en: They're trying to hit the sweet spot when they've been on the market long enough for the drug maker to make a tidy profit, but not so late that there's already generic competition.
sentences.zh: 他们试图找到一个最佳平衡点：药物上市时间足够长，让制药商赚取了可观的利润，但又没有晚到出现仿制药竞争。

sentences.en: So, it's kind of a Goldilocks phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 所以，这有点像“金发姑娘”现象。

sentences.en: Not too early, not too late.
sentences.zh: 不太早，也不太晚。

sentences.en: And the idea behind that is that they want to give drug makers the opportunity to make money
sentences.zh: 其背后的理念是，他们希望给制药商机会，让他们从创新中获利，

sentences.en: off of their innovation, to encourage risk-taking, to encourage investment in expensive clinical trials.
sentences.zh: 以鼓励冒险，鼓励对昂贵的临床试验进行投资。

sentences.en: But they don't want to wait so long that the drug has already started facing generic competition.
sentences.zh: 但他们不想等太久，以至于药物已经面临仿制药的竞争。

sentences.en: Because, in theory, that competition would drive down the price.
sentences.zh: 因为理论上，这种竞争会压低价格。

sentences.en: So, there wouldn't be as much of a point of having Medicare negotiate lower prices.
sentences.zh: 那样的话，让联邦医疗保险谈判降低价格就没有太大意义了。

sentences.en: So, Rebecca, how do you think this is going to affect Medicare patients?
sentences.zh: 那么，丽贝卡，你认为这对联邦医疗保险患者会有什么影响？

sentences.en: I mean, are they going to start paying less for their medications?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们开始支付更少的药费了吗？

sentences.en: So, the government is the big winner here in terms of savings because the government carries most of the burden of paying for the drugs that are taken by Medicare patients.
sentences.zh: 政府是节省成本方面的最大赢家，因为政府承担了联邦医疗保险患者所用药物的大部分费用。

sentences.en: The Congressional Budget Office estimates that the government will save nearly $100 billion over a decade.
sentences.zh: 国会预算办公室估计，政府在十年内将节省近1000亿美元。

sentences.en: But if the government's paying less, that can ultimately have trickle-down effects for patients.
sentences.zh: 但如果政府支付的费用减少，最终可能会对患者产生连锁反应。

sentences.en: And patients pay for their drugs in the form of paying insurance premiums and paying out-of-pocket costs when they pick up a prescription at the pharmacy.
sentences.zh: 患者通过支付保险费以及在药房取药时支付自付费用来购买药物。

sentences.en: And the idea is that if Medicare is saving money on these drugs, premiums will go down and patients will pay less out-of-pocket.
sentences.zh: 其理念是，如果联邦医疗保险在这些药物上节省了资金，保费就会下降，患者的自付费用也会减少。

sentences.en: Premiums will go down because premium is a portion of the drug cost, right?
sentences.zh: 保费会下降，因为保费是药品成本的一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: And the portion will be lower because the cost is lower.
sentences.zh: 而且由于成本降低，这一部分也会降低。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there's also another part of the Biden administration's effort to tackle drug prices.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府在应对药品价格方面还有另一项努力。

sentences.en: And that's a cap on the money that Medicare patients have to pay out-of-pocket when they pick up prescriptions at the pharmacy counter.
sentences.zh: 那就是对联邦医疗保险患者在药房取药时必须支付的自付费用设定上限。

sentences.en: Starting in 2025, the yearly spending will be capped at $2,000 per patient.
sentences.zh: 从2025年开始，每位患者的年度支出上限为2000美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's presumably much lower than many patients had been spending.
sentences.zh: 这想必比许多患者之前的支出要低得多。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That can make a huge difference financially for many patients.
sentences.zh: 这对许多患者来说，在经济上可能会产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And experts are saying that the Medicare negotiation savings may ultimately help fund that cap on out-of-pocket costs.
sentences.zh: 专家表示，联邦医疗保险谈判节省的资金最终可能有助于资助这一自付费用上限。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: So in a way, it could be actually quite direct, but through the savings that comes from the bargaining.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，这可能非常直接，但通过的是谈判带来的节省。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And remember, it's still really early days in this process.
sentences.zh: 请记住，这个过程还处于非常早期的阶段。

sentences.en: The negotiated prices under the program won't take effect until 2026.
sentences.zh: 该计划下的谈判价格要到2026年才会生效。

sentences.en: So that's the first year that the government would be seeing savings.
sentences.zh: 所以那是政府看到节省资金的第一年。

sentences.en: And it's also the very first step in what's going to turn out to be an annual process.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个年度过程的第一步。

sentences.en: Each year, the government will add new drugs to the list, while some drugs will fall off the list because generic competition has reached the market.
sentences.zh: 每年，政府都会将新药加入清单，同时一些药物会因为仿制药竞争进入市场而从清单中剔除。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's Medicare.
sentences.zh: 好的，那是联邦医疗保险。

sentences.en: But how do we expect this to affect the rest of the health care system, like everybody else?
sentences.zh: 但我们预计这会如何影响医疗保健系统的其他部分，比如其他人呢？

sentences.en: Like, say, I'm not on Medicare.
sentences.zh: 比如，假设我没有参加联邦医疗保险。

sentences.en: Will this affect me?
sentences.zh: 这会影响我吗？

sentences.en: So in theory, this program has no impact on the prices paid for medications taken by privately insured people.
sentences.zh: 理论上，该计划对私人保险人员所用药物的价格没有影响。

sentences.en: That said, in practice, it may open the door for lower prices in the private market, too.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，在实践中，它也可能为私营市场降低价格打开大门。

sentences.en: And that's because of a peculiarity in the way that drug prices are negotiated.
sentences.zh: 这是因为药品价格谈判方式中的一个特殊性。

sentences.en: So the way that drug pricing works is it's kept secret.
sentences.zh: 药品定价的工作方式是保密的。

sentences.en: The prices that different customers pay when you account for discounts and rebates are ultimately kept confidential.
sentences.zh: 当考虑到折扣和回扣时，不同客户支付的价格最终是保密的。

sentences.en: So let's walk through a hypothetical.
sentences.zh: 让我们做一个假设。

sentences.en: If I'm a drug manufacturer making, say, an arthritis drug, I am ultimately charging different prices to different customers.
sentences.zh: 如果我是一家制药商，生产一种关节炎药物，我最终会向不同的客户收取不同的价格。

sentences.en: And my different customers don't know how much the others are paying.
sentences.zh: 而我不同的客户并不知道其他人支付了多少。

sentences.en: And when Medicare's lower prices are made public, that adds a new lever for the buyers.
sentences.zh: 当联邦医疗保险的较低价格公开时，这为买家增加了一个新的筹码。

sentences.en: They'll be in a position where they can say, I want this same discount.
sentences.zh: 他们将处于一个可以要求“我也想要同样的折扣”的位置。

sentences.en: And if not, I will just withdraw my business, especially in a class like arthritis drugs.
sentences.zh: 如果不行，我就撤销业务，特别是在关节炎药物这类产品中。

sentences.en: There are a lot of other options.
sentences.zh: 还有很多其他的选择。

sentences.en: And that's something that these buyers can use to their advantage.
sentences.zh: 而这正是买家可以利用的优势。

sentences.en: So it basically gives buyers a kind of baseline for a negotiating position, right?
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上为买家提供了一个谈判的基准，对吧？

sentences.en: Something to point to and ask for.
sentences.zh: 一个可以作为依据并提出要求的筹码。

sentences.en: Suddenly, they have these x-ray glasses, if you will.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他们就有了这种“透视眼镜”，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: And now that they have that power, you know, if I'm the buyer, I can go to some other drug on the market that fills the same need because there are a lot of them.
sentences.zh: 既然他们有了这种权力，你知道，如果我是买家，我可以转向市场上其他能满足同样需求的药物，因为这类药物有很多。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Even though we're talking about drugs that are under patent and don't have generic competition, there are other options, other drugs available that fill the same need.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们讨论的是处于专利期内、没有仿制药竞争的药物，但市场上还有其他选择，其他能满足同样需求的药物。

sentences.en: OK, so this could lead to savings for Medicare and for private insurance.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以这可能会为联邦医疗保险（Medicare）和私人保险节省开支。

sentences.en: But obviously, this money is coming from somewhere, right?
sentences.zh: 但显然，这笔钱总得有个来源，对吧？

sentences.en: So what do we expect is going to happen to the pharma industry as a result?
sentences.zh: 那么我们预计制药行业会因此发生什么呢？

sentences.en: So the drug industry has been fighting the Medicare negotiation program.
sentences.zh: 制药行业一直在抵制联邦医疗保险的谈判计划。

sentences.en: The pharmaceutical company known as Merck has filed a lawsuit against the federal government following the paSt.
sentences.zh: 默克制药公司（Merck）在法案通过后已对联邦政府提起诉讼。

sentences.en: They've filed lawsuits trying to block the Biden administration from implementing it.
sentences.zh: 他们提起了诉讼，试图阻止拜登政府实施该计划。

sentences.en: Saying that being forced to negotiate drug prices with Medicare is, quote, tantamount to extortion.
sentences.zh: 称被迫与联邦医疗保险进行药价谈判，引用他们的话说，等同于勒索。

sentences.en: Arguing that, quote, the program takes property for public use without just compensation and violence.
sentences.zh: 他们辩称，引用他们的话说，该计划在没有公正补偿的情况下征用财产，且具有暴力性。

sentences.en: And they've warned that if it's implemented, it will have unintended consequences that could really harm patients.
sentences.zh: 他们还警告说，如果实施该计划，将会产生意想不到的后果，可能真正伤害到患者。

sentences.en: Drug manufacturers say it will result in loss of profits that will force them to pull back on developing groundbreaking new treatments.
sentences.zh: 制药商表示，这将导致利润损失，迫使他们缩减对开创性新疗法的研发投入。

sentences.en: They're saying it will lead to fewer cures.
sentences.zh: 他们说这会导致治愈手段减少。

sentences.en: It will lead to delays in patients getting certain medications.
sentences.zh: 这会导致患者获取某些药物的时间延迟。

sentences.en: It will discourage companies from developing the kinds of medications that are important and widely used by seniors.
sentences.zh: 这将阻碍公司开发那些对老年人重要且广泛使用的药物。

sentences.en: And, Rebecca, what do you make of those claims, the things the industry is arguing?
sentences.zh: 那么，丽贝卡，你如何看待这些说法，即行业提出的那些论点？

sentences.en: How much water do they actually hold?
sentences.zh: 它们的说服力到底有多大？

sentences.en: So I think one thing we know from health policy is that new laws will create new incentives.
sentences.zh: 我认为从卫生政策中我们知道的一点是，新法律会创造新的激励机制。

sentences.en: And for-profit companies are going to act accordingly to try to preserve their profits.
sentences.zh: 而营利性公司会采取相应行动，试图维护自己的利润。

sentences.en: And I do think the devil is in the details in terms of how this legislation was written.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为，这项立法在细节上暗藏玄机。

sentences.en: So notably, it discourages companies from developing the old-school synthetic drugs, the traditional pill you're most familiar with,
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，它阻碍了公司开发老派的合成药物，也就是你最熟悉的那种传统药丸，

sentences.en: and encourages them to develop the more expensive living cell drugs that dominate the list of most expensive medications today.
sentences.zh: 却鼓励他们开发更昂贵的活细胞药物，而这类药物目前占据了最昂贵药物名单的主导地位。

sentences.en: So in a way, in a kind of unexpected way, this could lead to more development of more expensive drugs.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上，以一种意想不到的方式，这可能会导致更多昂贵药物的研发。

sentences.en: That's certainly possible.
sentences.zh: 这当然是有可能的。

sentences.en: I think the way in which the drug industry responds to this new marketplace will dictate whether the goals of the program will ultimately be realized.
sentences.zh: 我认为制药行业对这个新市场的反应方式，将决定该计划的目标最终能否实现。

sentences.en: But I think beyond just the dollars and cents involved, there's something bigger happening here.
sentences.zh: 但我认为除了涉及的金钱利益之外，这里正在发生一些更重大的事情。

sentences.en: And this is, I think, why this is such an important news story, because there's a really fundamental shift taking place here in how prices are set in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么这是一个如此重要的新闻故事，因为美国在定价方式上正在发生根本性的转变。

sentences.en: It's opening a door that until now had ultimately been shut.
sentences.zh: 它打开了一扇直到现在还一直关闭着的大门。

sentences.en: We're starting with just this list of 10 initial products.
sentences.zh: 我们先从这最初的10种产品名单开始。

sentences.en: But the introduction of negotiation in this very limited slice of the market could ultimately lead to other huge changes.
sentences.zh: 但在这一非常有限的市场领域引入谈判，最终可能会导致其他巨大的变化。

sentences.en: It could open the door for the government to start negotiating drugs earlier in the life cycle of these products.
sentences.zh: 它可能会为政府打开大门，开始在这些产品生命周期的更早阶段进行药物谈判。

sentences.en: You know, when manufacturers have had fewer years enjoying a monopoly, it might ultimately lead to legislation that would mandate the same process in the private market.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当制造商享受垄断的时间变短时，这最终可能会促成强制私人市场采取同样流程的立法。

sentences.en: So I think this is a really fundamental shift in the way that drug pricing works in the United States, and we're in really uncharted waters.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是美国药品定价方式的根本性转变，我们正处于真正未知的领域。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's not just a list of 10 drugs.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是10种药物的名单。

sentences.en: It's the beginning of a whole new process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个全新流程的开始。

sentences.en: The government actually changing its relationship to the pharmaceutical industry.
sentences.zh: 政府实际上正在改变其与制药行业的关系。

sentences.en: In a way, opening, from pharma's perspective, this Pandora's box.
sentences.zh: 从制药行业的角度来看，这在某种程度上打开了潘多拉魔盒。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is a big part of the reason the drug industry has fought this program so hard.
sentences.zh: 这也是制药行业如此强烈抵制该计划的一个重要原因。

sentences.en: It's a real existential threat to their core of their business model, which, you know,
sentences.zh: 这对他们商业模式的核心构成了真正的生存威胁，你知道，

sentences.en: really hinges on extremely high prices relative to the rest of the world in the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们的商业模式确实依赖于美国相对于世界其他地区极高的价格。

sentences.en: I think another point that's important here is that the Medicare negotiation program is really an experiment.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里另一个重要的点是，联邦医疗保险的谈判计划实际上是一个实验。

sentences.en: And it's shaping up to be a test of the argument that the drug industry is making, that the sky will fall if Medicare has the ability to negotiate the prices of drugs.
sentences.zh: 它正在成为对制药行业论点的一次检验，即如果联邦医疗保险有权谈判药价，天就会塌下来。

sentences.en: If we see that the sky does not fall, that the drug industry continues to remain profitable and produce cures and the lower prices take effect, well, then we'll have our answer.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看到天并没有塌下来，制药行业继续保持盈利并生产治愈药物，且更低的价格开始生效，那么我们就会得到答案。

sentences.en: And that's an answer that will ripple throughout the American health care system.
sentences.zh: 而这个答案将波及整个美国医疗保健系统。

sentences.en: Rebecca, thank you.
sentences.zh: 丽贝卡，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的“Connections”谜题，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责创作“Spelling Bee”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你们刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该知道的消息。

sentences.en: This is the thick of it.
sentences.zh: 现在正处于最激烈的时刻。

sentences.en: We are in the middle of it right now.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于风暴中心。

sentences.en: You can hear that roar.
sentences.zh: 你能听到那咆哮声。

sentences.en: The whole roof just came off the house, Mike.
sentences.zh: 整个屋顶都被掀翻了，迈克。

sentences.en: Idalia, the first storm to pummel Florida this season, made landfall as a Category 3 hurricane at 7.45 a.m.
sentences.zh: 伊达利亚（Idalia）是本季袭击佛罗里达州的第一场风暴，于上午7点45分以三级飓风强度登陆，

sentences.en: in Taylor County, southeast of Tallahassee.
sentences.zh: 地点在塔拉哈西东南部的泰勒县。

sentences.en: It inundated coastal villages, carrying rain and storm surge, with winds near 125 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 它淹没了沿海村庄，带来了降雨和风暴潮，风速接近每小时125英里。

sentences.en: But by late Wednesday afternoon, it had weakened to a tropical storm and moved to Georgia and then into South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 但到周三下午晚些时候，它已减弱为热带风暴，并移向佐治亚州，随后进入南卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: Authorities in Florida reported two deaths from car crashes that were attributed to weather conditions, but said that across the state, the damage was less severe than expected.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州当局报告了两起因天气状况导致的交通事故死亡事件，但表示在全州范围内，损失比预期的要小。

sentences.en: And a wave of drones exploded in six separate regions of Russia overnight on Wednesday,
sentences.zh: 周三夜间，一波无人机袭击了俄罗斯的六个不同地区，

sentences.en: in an apparent sign that Ukraine was increasingly capable of striking deep inside Moscow's territory.
sentences.zh: 这显然表明乌克兰越来越有能力深入打击莫斯科境内。

sentences.en: Around the same time, Russia unleashed an aerial assault on at least three regions of Ukraine,
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时间，俄罗斯对乌克兰至少三个地区发动了空中袭击，

sentences.en: including one of the most significant barrages the Kiev region has experienced in months.
sentences.zh: 其中包括基辅地区几个月来经历的最严重的轰炸之一。

sentences.zh: 包含玛丽安·洛萨诺和黛安·黄的原创音乐。

sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德进行工程制作。

sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。

sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《Metro》的最新一集中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.zh: 在你获取播客的任何地方收听。
